text:
sarah: FYI support forwarded an urgent customer report — dedicated pool 'dp-84' saw a ~60% throughput drop starting ~00:10 UTC. Customer observed repeated 429s and a handful of 502s, and overall p50/p95 latencies doubled. They say model/version pinned to `redwood-v2-3` and pool id attached. Asking for triage and temporary mitigation.
autoscale-bot: ALERT: autoscaler rejected scale-up for pool dp-84 due to quota limit `max_instances=12` reached for org org-998. Reason: billing_hold=true. (request_id=az-9932)
raj: Can someone paste the pool id and the exact times? I'll pull batcher and queue metrics. Also can we get the customer's request headers for routing info? @mike @elena
sarah: pool dp-84, org-998, customer reported spike at 2026-03-16T00:10:12Z -> 00:18:44Z. Support attached sample request (sanitized) showing a streaming chat call with 1.2k token context and max_new_tokens=512.
raj: quick checks: running queries against metrics.
```
# prometheus queries
sum(rate(inference_requests_total{pool="dp-84"}[5m])) by (tenant)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_latency_seconds_bucket{pool="dp-84"}[5m])) by (le))
avg(batcher_queue_depth{pool="dp-84"})
```
raj: findings: QPS for tenant T-451 dropped from 14 -> 5. median batch_size dropped 7 -> 2. queue_depth increased from avg 1.2 -> 4.8. Prefill backlog increased simultaneously. Looks like small batches and higher queueing.
elena: hypothesis: scheduler/continuous-batcher started emitting many tiny batches — I see a change in behavior around the same time as a runtime config tweak earlier this week. Tiny batches blow throughput on large-context requests. Also saw high GPU util on one pod (98%) and very low on others — noisy neighbor + unfair token packing.
mike: I pushed a scheduler tweak 48h ago to be more conservative on max-latency targets. Commit: 9f4b2c7. Patch reduced `max_batch_tokens` from `8192` -> `2048` and lowered `target_batch_fill` from `0.9` -> `0.6`.
```
# /etc/redwood/runtime/scheduler.yaml (excerpt)
max_batch_tokens: 2048
target_batch_fill: 0.6
min_batch_tokens: 32
```
raj: that matches the observed median batch size collapse. For long-context chat (1.2k tokens), dropping max batch tokens forces smaller groupings and increases KV cache pressure — prefill becomes less efficient.
sarah: customer also mentioned intermittent 429s with "throttled by scheduler" message in body. Could that be our fair-share enforcement + the new max_instances cap? They were on a bursty workload at midnight.
elena: yes — two things converged: billing hold (preventing autoscale) + scheduler config that prioritizes latency by slicing batches. Net effect: fewer tokens per GPU per second and a hot pod (noisy tenant) stealing capacity.
mike: agree. Proposed immediate steps:
- roll back `max_batch_tokens` to 8192 (fast rollback) OR tweak `target_batch_fill` -> 0.85
- increase `min_batch_tokens` to 128 to avoid micro-batches for chat flows
- add a temporary tenant throttling rule to limit T-451 burst until we stabilize
- request billing to clear hold so autoscaler can add instances if needed
raj: for repro, here's a minimal script to simulate customer pattern (run from a test VM in same region):
```
for i in `seq 1 200`; do
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-v2-3","context_tokens":1200,"max_new_tokens":512,"stream":false}' &
done
```
Expected: median batch size >=6 and p95 latency < 700ms. Observed (on prod): median batch size ~2 and p95 latency ~1.8s, with occasional 429s.
sarah: can someone patch and run the repro against a canary pool? I'd prefer rolling rollback to be safe.
mike: I'll open a canary rollout to dp-84-canary, apply `max_batch_tokens=8192` and `min_batch_tokens=128` now. ETA 8m.
elena: temporary mitigation until canary: add tenant-level rate limit for T-451: `burst=30r/s` `sustained=8r/s` via route policy. Also create a short-lived rule to move heavy streaming requests to a separate shard so they don't fragment normal packing.
billing: Hi — confirmed org-998 had a payment issue; automated billing system set `billing_hold=true` on 2026-03-16T00:05Z which triggered capacity cap. Payment cleared at 00:42Z after we processed the invoice retry. Quota `max_instances` lifted at 00:44Z.
mike: good — once billing lift propagated autoscaler will be allowed to add instances. But we should still roll back scheduler change to recover throughput faster.
raj: monitoring output post-canary (t+12m): dp-84-canary median batch_size bumped to 6.5, p95 latency down to 780ms, queue_depth back to ~1.4 for canary. Main pool still catching up but scaling events are happening now that billing hold removed.
sarah: plan recap for support and CSM:
- billing resolved (billing) ✅
- canary rollback applied (mike) ✅
- tenant rate-limits applied (elena) ✅
- monitor 2h for regressions, auto-escalate if p95>1s or error_rate>0.5% (raj)
sarah: I'll update the customer with this timeline and ask them to validate expected throughput. Thanks all :pray:
mike: +1. I'll open a follow-up PR to add a test that simulates long-context chat load so we don't regress `max_batch_tokens` silently.
elena: also adding an alert that combines "median_batch_size" drop + "queue_depth" increase to catch this earlier. :eyes:
sarah: closing channel after 2h if stable.
